purpose: Define how Task-9 resource and effort fields are measured, attributed, preserved, and reported before concrete values or practical-value conclusions are produced.

rules: Do not derive elapsed duration solely from non-monotonic wall-clock timestamps when monotonic timing is available.
Record timeout and interruption outcomes explicitly.
Preserve runtime spent by failed executions if resources were actually consumed.
Direct telemetry is preferred over reconstructed estimates.
If utilization-adjusted compute cannot be measured, preserve device-time separately rather than invent utilization.
Shared-device attribution requires an explicit allocation rule.
Current hardware pricing must not be retroactively applied as historical observed cost without explicit estimation labeling.
Provider-reported token counts take precedence when they define billing.
Tokenizer reconstruction must record tokenizer identity and version.
Input, output, and cache-related token categories remain separate when the provider distinguishes them.
Unknown token usage remains unknown rather than zero.
Retries are preserved rather than removed from cost accounting.
Failed calls that consume billable or execution resources remain counted.
Tool calls and model calls remain separate fields.
Peak and cumulative quantities must not be conflated.
Temporary artifacts may be separately classified but must not be silently excluded when materially relevant.
Observed provider charges and reconstructed charges must be labeled separately.
A later rate card must not silently replace the rate applicable to an earlier run.
Currency conversion requires a separately preserved FX source and timestamp when conversion is performed.
Human effort is not monetized by default.
Active effort and elapsed session time remain separate.
Automated waiting time is not silently counted as active human effort.
Manual interventions must be recorded for both candidate and comparator sides.
Failed tuning attempts remain part of opportunity accounting.
Retrospective estimates are allowed only when clearly labeled and must not be represented as direct measurements.
Adaptation cost remains separate from ordinary evaluation cost.
Rollback cost is measured separately when rollback is executed.
Pre-existing training cost is not silently reclassified as deployment adaptation cost.
Adaptation examples and labels are information-opportunity evidence as well as resource evidence.
Allocation method must be frozen before using shared-resource values in a consequential comparison.
UNRESOLVED_SHARED_RESOURCE cannot be converted to zero.
A quality improvement does not automatically imply practical value.
A lower resource value does not automatically compensate for a failed hard quality or safety requirement.
Pareto domination may be reported only over explicitly comparable measured dimensions.
A weighted utility or cost-benefit score requires a predeclared formula and weights before applicable protected outcomes.
Missing values remain visible and cannot improve a practical-value conclusion by omission.
